questions.questionText: Which organisation is part of the accommodation sector of travel and tourism?
options: A hotel
An airline
A visitor information centre
A theme park
questions.correctAnswer: A hotel
questions.explanation: Hotels provide overnight lodging and related guest services, placing them in the accommodation sector.

curriculum.objective: Analyse relationships among tourism sectors, destination appeal, accessibility and visitor motivation.

questions.questionText: A new direct rail link reduces travel time to a rural destination by half. Which effect is most likely first?
options: The destination’s climate becomes cooler and less seasonal
Its accessibility and potential visitor market increase
All local prices immediately fall
Seasonality disappears completely
questions.correctAnswer: Its accessibility and potential visitor market increase
questions.explanation: Lower journey time reduces a key access barrier and makes the destination practical for more origin markets and shorter trips.

curriculum.subskill: Predict the effect of transport improvement
curriculum.objective: Analyse relationships among tourism sectors, destination appeal, accessibility and visitor motivation.

questions.questionText: Which visitor is mainly motivated by visiting friends and relatives?
options: A delegate attending a trade fair
A skier booking a two-week mountain package for winter recreation
A graduate staying with an aunt during a family celebration
A researcher surveying a national park
questions.correctAnswer: A graduate staying with an aunt during a family celebration
questions.explanation: The primary purpose is spending time with family, which is classified as visiting friends and relatives rather than leisure or business.

curriculum.objective: Analyse relationships among tourism sectors, destination appeal, accessibility and visitor motivation.

questions.questionText: A destination has strong cultural attractions but declining international arrivals after its only long-haul airline withdraws. Which response best addresses the immediate constraint?
options: Replace cultural attractions with offices
Stop marketing to every visitor segment
Raise attraction prices without research
Develop connecting-air and regional-rail partnerships with coordinated packages
questions.correctAnswer: Develop connecting-air and regional-rail partnerships with coordinated packages
questions.explanation: The attractions remain strong; the binding weakness is access, so integrated alternative transport links directly address the decline.

curriculum.subskill: Match strategy to an access weakness
curriculum.objective: Analyse relationships among tourism sectors, destination appeal, accessibility and visitor motivation.

questions.questionText: Which is an environmental cost of overcrowding at a natural attraction?
options: Erosion of paths and habitats
Higher employment in local cafés
More cultural exchange
Increased tax revenue
questions.correctAnswer: Erosion of paths and habitats
questions.explanation: Heavy visitor pressure can damage soil, vegetation and wildlife habitat, making erosion an environmental cost.

curriculum.objective: Evaluate economic, environmental and sociocultural tourism impacts and recommend responsible management responses.

questions.questionText: Why can a locally owned guesthouse create a stronger multiplier effect than an imported all-inclusive resort?
options: It prevents visitors from spending
More revenue is likely to be re-spent through local wages and suppliers
It guarantees zero environmental impact
All its guests must be domestic
questions.correctAnswer: More revenue is likely to be re-spent through local wages and suppliers
questions.explanation: Local ownership and purchasing keep a larger share of visitor spending circulating in the destination economy instead of leaking out.

curriculum.objective: Evaluate economic, environmental and sociocultural tourism impacts and recommend responsible management responses.

questions.questionText: A historic district is crowded for three hours each afternoon. Which management response most directly spreads visitor pressure?
options: Close every attraction permanently
Advertise only the busiest period
Use timed tickets and promote alternative routes and times
Remove all visitor information signs
questions.correctAnswer: Use timed tickets and promote alternative routes and times
questions.explanation: Capacity controls and spatial-temporal dispersal reduce peak concentration while maintaining access and visitor spending.

curriculum.objective: Evaluate economic, environmental and sociocultural tourism impacts and recommend responsible management responses.

questions.questionText: A marine tour creates jobs but boat noise disrupts breeding animals. Which policy best balances benefits and conservation?
options: Ban all coastal employment
Allow unlimited boats throughout the year
Move breeding animals to an artificial display
Set seasonal exclusion zones, vessel limits and local operator permits
questions.correctAnswer: Set seasonal exclusion zones, vessel limits and local operator permits
questions.explanation: Targeted limits protect sensitive breeding periods while permits preserve controlled economic participation for local operators.

curriculum.objective: Evaluate economic, environmental and sociocultural tourism impacts and recommend responsible management responses.

questions.questionText: What should a front-desk employee do first when a guest calmly reports a room problem?
options: Listen carefully and clarify the problem
Explain why the guest is mistaken
Transfer the guest without speaking
Promise compensation before checking facts
questions.correctAnswer: Listen carefully and clarify the problem
questions.explanation: Active listening establishes the facts, shows respect and provides the basis for an appropriate service-recovery response.

curriculum.objective: Apply customer-service principles to diverse visitor needs, service recovery and quality management situations.

questions.questionText: A traveller using a wheelchair asks about an excursion. Which response demonstrates inclusive service?
options: Assume the excursion is unsuitable
Ask about specific access needs and verify facilities with the operator
Tell a companion to decide
Offer only the most expensive alternative
questions.correctAnswer: Ask about specific access needs and verify facilities with the operator
questions.explanation: The response avoids assumptions, centres the traveller’s needs and checks accurate operational information before recommending an option.

curriculum.objective: Apply customer-service principles to diverse visitor needs, service recovery and quality management situations.

questions.questionText: Which indicator best measures whether a service-recovery process resolves complaints effectively?
options: The colour of staff uniforms
The number of brochures printed
Repeat-complaint rate and post-resolution satisfaction
The age of the reception desk
questions.correctAnswer: Repeat-complaint rate and post-resolution satisfaction
questions.explanation: These measures show whether the underlying issue was solved and whether the customer judged the recovery positively.

curriculum.objective: Apply customer-service principles to diverse visitor needs, service recovery and quality management situations.

questions.questionText: A flight cancellation leaves a family at an airport overnight. Which response best demonstrates empowered service recovery?
options: Tell the family to search online without assistance
Wait until the next shift before recording the case
Offer an apology but no practical action
Confirm entitlements, arrange available accommodation and transport, and document follow-up
questions.correctAnswer: Confirm entitlements, arrange available accommodation and transport, and document follow-up
questions.explanation: The response combines accurate information, immediate practical support, ownership and continuity rather than offering words alone.

curriculum.objective: Apply customer-service principles to diverse visitor needs, service recovery and quality management situations.

questions.questionText: Which element of the marketing mix refers to how customers obtain or access a tourism product?
options: Place
Price
Promotion
Product
questions.correctAnswer: Place
questions.explanation: Place covers distribution channels and points of access, such as direct booking, travel agents and online platforms.

curriculum.objective: Use market research, segmentation and the marketing mix to develop and evaluate tourism products.

questions.questionText: A museum wants to understand why local teenagers rarely visit. Which research method gives the most directly relevant insight?
options: Count overseas visitors only
Run focus groups with local teenagers
Copy another museum’s prices
Survey staff members only about their own leisure interests
questions.correctAnswer: Run focus groups with local teenagers
questions.explanation: Speaking with the target non-user segment can reveal attitudes, barriers and product ideas that attendance totals cannot explain.

curriculum.objective: Use market research, segmentation and the marketing mix to develop and evaluate tourism products.

questions.questionText: A tour operator targets retired travellers who prefer slower itineraries and cultural learning. Which segmentation bases are being used?
options: Geographic only
Income only
Demographic and psychographic
Random and seasonal
questions.correctAnswer: Demographic and psychographic
questions.explanation: Retirement is demographic, while preferences for pace and cultural learning describe lifestyle and interests, which are psychographic.

curriculum.objective: Use market research, segmentation and the marketing mix to develop and evaluate tourism products.

questions.questionText: Research shows eco-conscious visitors value local food but consider the current package too expensive. Which product decision best responds to both findings?
options: Remove all local suppliers and increase price
Market the unchanged package more aggressively
Add luxury transfers that raise costs
Offer a shorter locally sourced package with transparent optional extras
questions.correctAnswer: Offer a shorter locally sourced package with transparent optional extras
questions.explanation: The redesigned core preserves the valued local feature while reducing base cost and allowing customers to control additional spending.

curriculum.objective: Use market research, segmentation and the marketing mix to develop and evaluate tourism products.

questions.questionText: What is the main purpose of a contingency plan in tour operations?
options: To define alternative actions if disruption occurs
To guarantee that no hazard can exist
To replace the published itinerary every day
To remove the need for staff communication
questions.correctAnswer: To define alternative actions if disruption occurs
questions.explanation: A contingency plan sets out practical responses and responsibilities so operations can continue safely when expected arrangements fail.

curriculum.objective: Plan feasible tourism operations by integrating itineraries, capacity, seasonality, risk and contingency decisions.

questions.questionText: A coach tour has 44 passengers, one driver and one guide. The attraction allows groups of no more than 25 people. What is required?
options: Cancel every booking
Arrange at least two timed visitor groups
Send all passengers through together
Remove the guide from the headcount without checking
questions.correctAnswer: Arrange at least two timed visitor groups
questions.explanation: The party exceeds the attraction’s group capacity, so splitting the visitors into coordinated entry groups is operationally necessary.

curriculum.objective: Plan feasible tourism operations by integrating itineraries, capacity, seasonality, risk and contingency decisions.

questions.questionText: A mountain excursion is scheduled during a period of rapidly changing weather. Which control is most appropriate?
options: Ignore forecasts once bookings close
Let each visitor choose an unrecorded route
Set weather thresholds, monitor forecasts and prepare a lower-risk alternative
Promise departure regardless of official warnings
questions.correctAnswer: Set weather thresholds, monitor forecasts and prepare a lower-risk alternative
questions.explanation: Defined decision thresholds, current information and a viable alternative reduce exposure while supporting a timely operational decision.

curriculum.objective: Plan feasible tourism operations by integrating itineraries, capacity, seasonality, risk and contingency decisions.

questions.questionText: An itinerary has a 40-minute airport transfer, but historic data show traffic delays of up to 35 minutes and check-in closes 20 minutes after planned arrival. What is the best revision?
options: Keep the timing because average traffic may be lighter
Reduce the transfer time shown to customers
Remove the airport check-in requirement
Add a buffer exceeding the observed delay and define a backup transfer option
questions.correctAnswer: Add a buffer exceeding the observed delay and define a backup transfer option
questions.explanation: The current plan has insufficient resilience; an evidence-based buffer plus backup transport protects the fixed check-in deadline.

curriculum.objective: Plan feasible tourism operations by integrating itineraries, capacity, seasonality, risk and contingency decisions.
